dedupe_keys.name: dtu skadesøkonomi flood damage cost model coherent project denmark

description: The DTU SkadesØkonomi (damage economics) model is a GIS-based model for estimating the costs of flooding from the sea in Denmark, developed at DTU Management with the consultancy LNH Water in the COHERENT coastal flooding project funded by Innovation Fund Denmark; its documentation and user guide were published on 15 April 2021. The documentation describes it as one of the most complete publicly available models for coastal flood damage costs in Denmark, also usable for cloudbursts if users supply building damage functions for that case. It is built on a GIS database of activities and physical assets and has sub-models for buildings (damage functions based on insurance data from storm Bodil in 2013), people and health, transport and traffic delays, industry and businesses, recreational values, ecosystems and biodiversity, tourism, critical infrastructure (identifying which assets are flooded, without costing them) and public services. Inputs are flooded areas from static sea level rise or dynamic storm surge models, with a default RCP 4.5 2050 100-year scenario from the DMI Klimaatlas, and national datasets that users can replace with municipal data. The model is open source but built in ArcGIS, so its use needs a software licence. Caveats: some sub-models only identify exposure, and some data are available only to municipalities. Coverage is Denmark. It supports hazard exposure and economic analysis of coastal flooding for buildings, roads and critical infrastructure; related records are the Danish high water statistics and Kystdata.
